setlist.title: Going Down the Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **To Lay Me Down** (3 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer calls Jerry's playing on To Lay Me Down quintessential; Reviewer found To Lay Me Down perfect, and the final segment slightly off [2][22][24][26]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer had hoped all day for the Scarlet>Fire and found it overwhelming; Reviewer calls the Scarlet/Fire and Estimated/Eyes pairings magic [6][20][22]
- **Ballad of a Thin Man** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer singles out Ballad of a Thin Man as awesome; Notes say this was the first time the band played Ballad of a Thin Man [2][24]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Reviewer found Little Red Rooster a lot of fun [25]
- **So What** (1 review): Jerry noodling on So What signaled to the reviewer that the second set would smoke [26]
- **Going Down the Road Feeling Bad** (1 review): Reviewer found the Going Down the Road coming out of space groovy [22]
- Reviewer found the Eyes a bit rushed [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **Ballad of a Thin Man**: rare: 10 archived performances [30]
- **To Lay Me Down**: back after 299 archived shows (1623 days) [30]
- **So What**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]

## The recordings

- **gd88-03-27.matrix.braverman.17262.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 146 min; rated 4.42/5 by 24 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the tape never quite earns a perfect score despite the show's brilliance; Reviewer says the matrix mix does the night justice; Reviewer says the mix blends audience and soundboard sources, giving the best of both [21][24][25]
- **gd1988-03-27.147999.fm.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: FM broadcast; 23 songs; 144 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1988-03-27.schoeps.unknown.gotfob.88250.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 146 min; rated 4.8/5 by 10 [4]. Said about its sound: A splice from the master falls where Bobby ends his first verse; three dropouts were removed [4]
- **gd1988-03-27.144487.sennme-80.porter.carbonetta.sirmick.flac1644**: source not stated; 23 songs; 147 min [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer felt the band sensed the crowd wanted a good time and delivered; the Dead seemed to love Hampton [18]
- Reviewer stood two people from the stage, right in front of Jerry [20]
- Bobby's pink wireless Ibanez failed, so the band jammed while waiting; he then sprinted out strumming the Sugar Magnolia intro [21]
- Reviewer feels the energy fizzles toward the end of the show [28]
- Reviewer stayed at the Days Inn across the street yet got lost finding the way back [29]
- The crowd's first 'Hey Now' answered Jerry instantly, showing the Hampton audience's intensity [29]
- Reviewer calls this the best show of 1988 and says Hampton brought out the Dead's best [27]
- Reviewer recommends also hearing the Jersey shows from this tour [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd88-03-27.matrix.braverman.17262.sbeok.shnf**: source: Ultramatrix (SBD/AUD mix). Lineage: DAT (Panasonic 3800)> CD (HHBCDR800)> EAC> SHN via Peter Braverman [1]
- **gd1988-03-27.147999.fm.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master In-House FM Cassettes; Sony D5M [2]. Also: Master cassette by Michael Hessberg, transferred by Charlie Miller; ultramatrix soundboard patches fill short gaps in To Lay Me Down>Let It Grow and Eyes [2]
- **gd1988-03-27.schoeps.unknown.gotfob.88250.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by gotfob; source: FOB > Schoeps Cmc3 + omni #3 > Dat @ 44.1k [4]
- **gd1988-03-27.144487.sennme-80.porter.carbonetta.sirmick.flac1644**: taped by Stephen Porter; transferred by Nick Carbonetta and SirMick; source: Sennheiser ME-80s > Sony D-5 > Master Cassette - Taped by Stephen Porter [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1988-03-27 Hampton Coliseum, Hampton, VA](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2018/10/grateful-dead-1988-03-27-hampton.html) [34]
